scams.name: Grand Palace ‘Closed’ Tuk-Tuk Gem Shop Tour
scams.description: You walk up to the Grand Palace entrance on Thanon Na Phra Lan and a friendly man in a pressed shirt — often introducing himself as a teacher or ‘palace officer’ — greets you with ‘Welcome! Where are you from?’ Before you can orient yourself he tells you the palace is ‘closed until 1pm for a royal ceremony’ and flags down a waiting *tuk-tuk* that will take you on a loop of ‘beautiful hidden temples’ for just 20 baht. A widely-cited r/ThailandTourism thread titled ‘I filmed the Grand Palace is closed scam in Bangkok’ documents the choreography: the first stop is a minor *wat*, the second is a ‘government tailor,’ the third is a gem shop where staff in suits produce ‘investment-grade’ sapphires with laminated certificates. A stone that retails for 1,500 baht on Silom is sold to you for 40,000.
scams.avoidance: Verify Grand Palace hours the same morning on royalgrandpalace.th or Google Maps before you leave the hotel. Enter through the main Visitor Centre gate on Na Phra Lan and ignore anyone who intercepts you walking in from the river or Sanam Luang. If a tuk-tuk quotes under 300 baht for any ‘tour,’ the driver’s revenue comes entirely from shop commissions — walk away. Buy suits only from tailors with posted prices and a decade of reviews (Tailor on Ten, Rajawongse on Sukhumvit Soi 4), never from a shop you were taken to. If you are already mid-tour, decline to enter any shop — the commission model collapses at the first refusal and the driver will drop you at your actual destination.
scams.location: Grand Palace, Wat Pho, Wat Arun, Chao Phraya riverfront entrances

scams.name: Suvarnabhumi Airport Taxi Meter Refusal
scams.description: You land at Suvarnabhumi, make it to the official taxi queue in the basement of Terminal 1, and get assigned Car 847. The driver nods, loads your bags, and says ‘500 baht to Sukhumvit, no meter.’ The legitimate metered fare to central Sukhumvit is 220–350 baht plus about 50 baht in tolls. At 2am and loaded with luggage, 500 baht feels manageable and you accept. You have just paid roughly double for a scam that r/Bangkok and r/ThailandTourism have logged in thousands of variants. The airport queue is governed by rules requiring meter use — but enforcement collapses between 11pm and 6am, exactly when jet-lagged tourists arrive.
scams.avoidance: Between 11pm and 6am, skip the airport taxi queue entirely and take the Airport Rail Link City Line (45 baht, 45 minutes to Phaya Thai). If you do take an airport taxi, say ‘meter, please — Motorway’ before you get in; if the driver refuses, walk to the next car and don’t argue. Use Grab or Bolt anywhere in the city — the fare is fixed in-app and the route is recorded, which eliminates meter games and padded detours. Know the expected fare before you open the door: BKK → Sukhumvit is 220–350 baht metered plus 45–75 baht in tolls; DMK → Sukhumvit is 300–400 baht. If a driver quotes a flat rate, photograph the license plate before walking away and report it to the Tourist Police on 1155 — they maintain a complaint database.
scams.location: Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK) arrivals level, Don Mueang (DMK), Sukhumvit hotel driveways

scams.name: Patpong / Soi Cowboy Ping Pong Show Drink Bill
scams.description: A tout on Patpong hands you a laminated menu: free entry, ‘100 baht beers,’ free show upstairs. The show is brief and strange. When you try to leave, staff slide between you and the door and a bill arrives for 8,000 baht. The drinks on the menu you were shown are not the drinks you were served; a second menu appears now, with small print charging 700 baht per beer and 2,000 baht per ‘lady drink’ you did not order. r/ThailandTourism ‘Horrifying Experience at Patpong Night Market’ describes exactly this — three staff standing between the tourist and the exit until the bill is paid in full. *Bangkok Post* ran a 2023 piece on a French tourist hit with an 87,000 baht bill at a Patpong ping-pong venue who paid because bouncers threatened violence.
scams.avoidance: If you want to see a ping-pong show, go in the early evening to a venue with Google Maps reviews, printed prices at the door, and other tourists already inside. Before you sit down, ask for a written total: ‘one show plus one beer, all in.’ If they won’t write a number, walk out. Don’t accept drinks offered to hostesses, tablemates, or staff — each one is billed to you at scam rates. Pay each drink at the bar as you order it, not on a tab. If a padded bill arrives and staff block you, call Tourist Police on 1155 on speaker — the number is answered 24/7 in English, and venues fold within minutes of the word ‘police.’
scams.location: Patpong Soi 1 & 2 (Silom), Soi Cowboy (Sukhumvit Soi 21), Nana Plaza alleys

scams.name: Tuk-Tuk Tailor Suit Scam
scams.description: You come out of Asok BTS and a well-dressed man falls into step: ‘My brother has a tailor shop. Sukhumvit 11, very good price. Tuk-tuk takes you for 50 baht, end-of-month special.’ At the shop, a charming tailor measures you up, recommends two suits in ‘Super 120 wool’ for 8,500 baht, and promises delivery in 48 hours. You pay cash. Two days later the suits arrive: the ‘wool’ is 40 percent polyester, the lining is acetate pretending to be silk, and the shoulders slope because the pattern was cut for a different body shape. By the time you notice, your flight is tomorrow. This is the classic Bangkok tailor scam — running since at least the 1980s and documented in almost every first-timer thread on r/ThailandTourism and r/Bangkok.
scams.avoidance: Research tailors before your trip on r/Bangkok and askandyaboutclothes.com; stick to shops with a decade of reputation (Rajawongse, Narry’s, Tailor on Ten, 9 Tailors). Never follow a tuk-tuk recommendation to any tailor — if the tailor needs a street tout, the revenue is in commissions, not craftsmanship. Pay by credit card in stages: a 20–30 percent deposit only, with the balance due on satisfactory final fitting. Ask to see the actual bolt of fabric and photograph the mill label before any cloth is cut; confirm the composition matches what you were quoted. Build at least five days between first fitting and your flight, so you have leverage to request corrections. If a tailor can’t work in that window, find another shop.
scams.location: Sukhumvit (Asok, Nana), Pratunam, around Hua Lamphong train station

scams.name: Fake Monk Donation Racket (Sukhumvit / Asok / Nana)
scams.description: Walking across the Asok BTS skywalk toward Terminal 21, a man in saffron robes steps in front of you holding a small bronze amulet and a donation book filled with names and amounts — 500 baht, 2,000 baht, $50. He presses the amulet into your hands, makes a brief blessing gesture, and points at the book. Social pressure takes over; you hand over 500 baht and feel good about it. You shouldn’t. r/ThailandTourism ‘Monks asking for money sukhumvit/Asoke’ documents the pattern and notes these crews now run in Buddhist countries, not just Europe and the US. Real Theravada monks do not solicit cash from tourists on public walkways — genuine alms-giving (*tak bat*) happens at dawn on the streets near their monastery and involves food, not money.
scams.avoidance: Real Thai monks do not solicit cash from tourists on the street. Decline with a polite *wai* and keep walking. If you want to make a temple donation, use the official metal donation box inside any *wat* — Wat Pho, Wat Arun, and Wat Benchamabophit all have them. Don’t accept any object placed in your hands by a ‘monk’; hand it back once without discussion or drop it and walk on. Legitimate morning alms-giving involves food offerings, never a donation book. Report persistent fake monks to the Tourist Police on 1155 or the Bangkok Metropolitan Police — they keep a database of active offenders.
scams.location: Asok and Nana BTS skywalks, Sukhumvit Soi 3–11, Chatuchak Weekend Market

scams.name: Grab / Bolt Cancel-and-Pay-Cash Switch
scams.description: You book a Grab from your hotel to Suvarnabhumi for 380 baht. The driver accepts, parks 200 meters away, and sends a chat message in broken English: ‘Please cancel booking. Pay me cash 800 baht now.’ You have 40 minutes until the airport express leaves. If you cancel, Grab records it as your cancellation — no refund, driver penalty waived, no fare record. If you refuse, the driver idles until the app auto-cancels you as a no-show and you get charged a cancellation fee anyway. r/ThailandTourism ‘Grab cancellation scam tip’ describes the pattern: drivers send scripted messages claiming motorbike accidents or traffic emergencies to pressure you into canceling and switching to cash at triple the fare.
scams.avoidance: Never cancel a Grab or Bolt booking on the driver’s request. Reply ‘app price only, thank you’ and wait for the ride to start. If the driver idles for five minutes without moving, cancel yourself from the app — the cancellation logs the driver’s behavior, and Grab or Bolt support will refund the fee and penalize the driver. At Suvarnabhumi, use the designated Grab pickup zone at Level 4 (Departures); Grab drivers can legally enter this zone. Keep screenshots of every booking — fare, route, driver ID — so you can claim documented overcharges through in-app support (typically refunded within 24 hours). Default to Grab over Bolt in Bangkok for tighter driver vetting, but neither is immune.
scams.location: Suvarnabhumi (BKK), Don Mueang (DMK), Sukhumvit Soi 11 & 23 pickup points

scams.name: Indian ‘Lucky Face’ Hair Supplement & Fortune Teller
scams.description: You walk out of Asok BTS and a well-dressed Indian man falls into step, smiles broadly, and says ‘You have a very lucky face, sir.’ He asks where you’re from, makes flattering predictions, then produces a small jar of ‘Ayurvedic hair-growth paste’ or a wallet of ‘certified gems’ — the pitch pivots depending on your reaction. By the time you realize you haven’t mentioned hair loss, he is asking for 1,500 baht for a ‘lucky blessing’ or 4,000 baht for a ‘guaranteed’ supplement. r/Bangkok catalogs the standard scripts; r/ThailandTourism ‘SCAM ALERT — Can I see your country’s currency?’ documents a parallel currency-view variant where the ‘lucky face’ compliment is followed by a request to see your local notes — the scammer either palms part of the stack or uses the view to gauge how much cash you are carrying.
scams.avoidance: Don’t stop walking when approached. Brief eye contact and ‘*mai ao krap*’ (men) or ‘*mai ao kha*’ (women) — literally ‘don’t want’ — works; sustained engagement does not. Never hand your wallet, phone, or cash to a stranger for any reason, including ‘just to look’ or ‘to demonstrate.’ If an item is placed in your hand, drop it on the ground or hand it back once without discussion and walk away. Real Ayurvedic practitioners work from clinics with addresses; street sellers are all running the same script. Photograph the tout from a distance and report to the Tourist Police on 1155 if the crew follows or escalates — they track active operators on Sukhumvit.
scams.location: Sukhumvit Soi 11, Silom Road, Khao San Road, Asok BTS exits

scams.name: Khao San Road Drink-Spiking & Pickpocket
scams.description: It’s 1am on Khao San Road and a bar pulls you in with buckets of rum-and-Red-Bull for 200 baht. You take two, chat with new friends, and wake up in a *tuk-tuk* with 19,500 baht missing from your wallet, no phone, and no memory of the last four hours. r/Bangkok ‘Drugged, robbed and given covid19 in Khao San Bangkok’ describes this incident almost word for word: the poster was spiked, removed from the bar, emptied, and tuk-tuk’d back to their hotel. Khao San hosts tens of thousands of backpackers nightly — the perfect cover — and Bangkok police have flagged the bucket cocktails (small plastic buckets filled with spirits and unknown mixers) as the delivery vehicle of choice.
scams.avoidance: Don’t accept a bucket cocktail. Order bottled beer, or a cocktail mixed in front of you at the bar. Watch your drink being made and keep it in your hand; discard any drink you set down. Travel in groups on Khao San — solo drinking here is the highest-risk scenario in Bangkok. Store your passport, extra cards, and most cash in the hotel safe and carry only 1,000–2,000 baht and one card. If you feel suddenly drunk beyond your drink count, text a trusted contact your location and head to the hotel immediately; a Grab is the safest exit.
scams.location: Khao San Road, Rambuttri, Soi Rambuttri, tuk-tuk trips to Khao San
